To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of the book is a function of the presence in books and that this is in turn a function of the interaction with the book.

(1) the sense of presence in books, films and VR is a subjective experience; (2) it is a multidimensional construct, consisting of different dimensions of presence; (3) it is a function of the technical immersion; and (4) it depends on the type of medium and the task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how presence can be influenced by the design of the virtual environment.
the question of how the quality of immersion in a virtual environment affects the sense of presence.
the question of what makes us experience the presence in books, film and VR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more realistic a virtual world is, the higher the sense of presence in this world is.
the sense of presence increases with an increase of immersion.
the better a VR system is in terms of sensory immersion, the more presence is experienced by the user.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sense of presence depends on the quality of immersion, but also on the quality of the story.
presence is not a function of the technical immersion, but of the quality of the experience.
the more immersive the system the higher the presence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sense of presence in virtual reality is not a function of immersion, but rather a function of the user's belief that he or she is in the virtual environment (Regenbrech & Schubert).
the quality of immersion is a necessary, but not sufficient condition for a high sense of presence.
the sense of presence does not only depend on the quality of the immersion, but also on the book problem, which is a function of the book problem.
